newsitem.title: USA: Dupont sets $4 billion alliance, employee transfers.
newsitem.headline: Dupont sets $4 billion alliance, employee transfers.

text.p: DuPont Co. said Wednesday it would pay $4 billion for consulting and computer services over the next decade in an unusual deal that calls for more than 3,000 employees to be transferred to the service providers.

The nation's largest chemical company said that under the alliances with Computer Sciences Corp. and Andersen Consulting, it would transfer 3,100 employees to those firms and retain 1,100 employees in its data systems operation.

DuPont Chief Information Officer Cinda Hallman said the DuPont workers to be offered jobs at Computer Sciences and Andersen would remain in the Wilmington, Del., area and would be offered "comparable" compensation and benefits.

In a telephone news conference, she declined to say how the 10-year, $4 billion contracts would be divided between the two companies, adding that the alliances would yield "5 to 10 percent cost improvements over time" for DuPont.
Hallman said the deal was different from traditional outsourcing because "DuPont was maintaining the role of leader and manager."

Under the agreement, El Segundo, Calif.-based Computer Sciences will manage DuPont's global mainframe and personal computer networks and its telecommunications system and be responsible for computer applications in Europe and Canada.
Andersen Consulting will provide DuPont with consulting services in manufacturing, marketing, distribution and other areas for the company's chemicals and energy businesses.
Hallman said DuPont had cut $500 million in costs from its information systems operations, a reduction of 40 percent since 1991.
"We've made it into a very lean and highly productive organisation. But we needed to take it to the next level," she said in an interview after the news conference.
The alliance would provide DuPont with access to more skills and technology and would further boost productivity, she said.
Computer Sciences, with about 40,000 employees and sales of $5.2 billion for the fiscal year ended in September, provides technology management and consulting services.
Andersen Consulting provides management and technology consulting to clients around the world.
In addition to making commodity chemicals and brand-name products such as Teflon for cookware coatings and Lycra for stretch fabrics, DuPont owns Conoco, a major oil producer.
DuPont stock fell $2.50 to $92.625 and Computer Sciences lost 50 cents to $84, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
